members.name: IsPlaying
members.signature: public static bool IsPlaying { get; set; }

docs.summary: True when the game is actively running (play mode in editor, or standalone player).

members.name: IsEditor
members.signature: public static bool IsEditor { get; set; }

docs.summary: True when running inside the editor (false in standalone builds).

members.name: IsHeadless
members.signature: public static bool IsHeadless { get; set; }

docs.summary: True when running without a window or graphics device (e.g. a dedicated server, or a build launched with --headless). Gameplay, physics and scripts still run; rendering does not.

members.name: IsPaused
members.signature: public static bool IsPaused { get; set; }

docs.summary: True when play mode is paused. Update/FixedUpdate/LateUpdate stop, but rendering continues.
Whether gameplay should execute this frame (playing and not paused, or stepping).

members.name: IsGameplayExecuting
members.signature: public static bool IsGameplayExecuting { get; set; }

docs.summary: True while gameplay code (Update/FixedUpdate) is executing. Used by the editor's input filtering to distinguish gameplay input from editor input.

members.name: TargetFrameRate
members.signature: public static int TargetFrameRate { get; set; }

docs.summary:
Frames per second the loop is paced to, whether that loop is the editor's, a standalone game's or a headless server's. Zero or less runs unlimited, which is what a game starts at until its own code says otherwise. This is a ceiling, so with [`VSync`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Application~VSync) on the lower of the two wins.

In the editor this belongs to the editor's own preferences until play mode starts, which hands it back to this default so the game's code decides, exactly as in a build.

members.name: VSync
members.signature: public static bool VSync { get; set; }

docs.summary: Whether a frame is held back until the display is ready for it, which caps the rate to the refresh rate and removes tearing. Off in a game until its own code turns it on, and on in the editor unless its preferences say otherwise. Has nothing to act on when [`IsHeadless`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Application~IsHeadless).

members.name: QuitHandler
members.signature: public static System.Action? QuitHandler { get; set; }

docs.summary: Replaces what [`Quit`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Application~Quit) does. The editor sets this so quitting stops play mode instead of closing the editor.

Quits the game. In the editor this stops play mode, in a headless run it ends the loop, and in a standalone build it closes the window. Gameplay code should call this rather than [`Quit`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Game~Quit).

members.name: DataPath
members.signature: public static string DataPath { get; set; }

docs.summary: Directory containing the running executable (standalone) or project root (editor). Used by PlayerAssetBackend to locate assets relative to the executable.
